routerd2 local changes to github.com/google/nftables
================================================

Upstream: https://github.com/google/nftables
Version: v0.3.0
Commit: 6f574e7fd1b4d07006d1c598cdb9b22789e5e541
Go module sum: h1:bkyZ0cbpVeMHXOrtlFc8ISmfVqq5gPJukoYieyVmITg=
Original archive: https://proxy.golang.org/github.com/google/nftables/@v/v0.3.0.zip
Original archive SHA256:
70c243170b087a106d2635674d012d12eafa93c3972a1c96f61460693faf418f

The existing upstream LICENSE and copyright headers are preserved. This tree
contains production Go packages, expr unit tests, and module metadata. Unrelated
upstream integration tests and their test-only helpers are omitted. UPSTREAM.json records the exact source and selection.

Modified files: expr/expr.go, conn.go
New regression tests: expr/masq_routerd2_test.go

The local patch sets NF_NAT_RANGE_PROTO_SPECIFIED when Masq.ToPorts is true,
and preserves Random, FullyRandom and Persistent flags alongside port ranges.
Linux nft_masq does not infer the flag from protocol-register attributes; the
unmodified library therefore encodes a port range that the kernel ignores.
The conn.go patch requests one success acknowledgement on the last batch
operation. Linux reports errors from every failed operation regardless of the
ACK flag, after committing or aborting the complete batch. Actual zone policies
reproduced ENOBUFS from per-operation success acknowledgements after commit.
A four-tunnel zone policy also overflowed the queue with the unused full-rule
echoes requested by NLM_F_ECHO. Flush suppresses those requests; it does not
consume or return their data. One success ACK retains atomicity and error
handling without raising socket limits or adding concurrent I/O.
The public API remains unchanged.

Reference for the kernel interfaces:
https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v6.8/net/netfilter/nfnetlink.c
https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v6.18/net/netfilter/nft_masq.c

Run the library regressions from the routerd2 module with:
    go test github.com/google/nftables/expr
The routerd2 isolated network integration test also exercises real IPv4/IPv6
UDP masquerade port ranges, DNAT/SNAT and atomic nftables table replacement.

The original module checksum identifies upstream, not this modified tree.
routerd2's generated license manifest records the local source tree digest
separately. This narrow replacement can be removed when a pinned upstream
release provides the same behavior and passes both regression gates.
